parts.problem_md:
Fig. 5.2 describes an agricultural project which has been introduced in part of China.

![Text describing a project involving Chinese farmers reducing fertiliser use by 1.2 million tons, preventing water pollution and saving $12.2 billion.](assets/001-text-describing-a-project-involving-chinese-farm.png)

*Fig 5.2*

Use evidence from Fig. 5.2 to show that this is a good example of sustainable agriculture.
parts.solution_md:
Provides enough food for the population due to increased yields. **[1]** Reduces the amount of fertiliser used. **[1}** Reduces environmental impact of fertiliser runoff. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is **'show'**; means that the answer must provide evidence from the written source to demonstrate that the strategies are sustainable social, economically or environmentally.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark **[1]** for each valid point (up to a maximum of 3 marks)
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Teaches farmers not to overuse fertilisers
> - Farmers can pass on knowledge about fertiliser use
> - Reduces the cost of food production
> - Saves on cost of fertilisers
> - Saved 12.2 billion US dollars

> **[exam-tip]**
> The key to gaining marks on this question is to highlight sustainability so ways in which food production can provide enough food whilst reducing the impact on the environment whilst reducing costs.

parts.problem_md:
Fig. 5.1 shows information about fertiliser use and cereal crop production in part of China.

![Graph showing fertiliser use and cereal crop production from 2004 to 2016. Fertiliser use rises steadily; crop production fluctuates, peaking around 2014.](assets/002-graph-showing-fertiliser-use-and-cereal-crop-pro.png)

*Fig 5.1*

What was the amount of cereal crop production in 2014?

**Extract:**

Fig. 5.1 shows information about fertiliser use and cereal crop production in part of China.

Describe the relationship between fertiliser use and cereal crop production shown in Fig. 5.1.
parts.solution_md:
Both fertiliser and cereal increased there is a positive correlation until 2014 **[1]** the more fertiliser that is used the higher the crop production.** [1]** 2004 – 2008 fertiliser 410–420 to 480 kg and cereal production 420 to 490m metric tonnes **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is **'describe'**; means that the answer must state the key points of a topic and provide its characteristics and main features.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark **[1]** for each valid point (up to a maximum of 3 marks)
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - 2004 – 2008 both increased (at the same rate)/directly proportional
> - Fertiliser rate continues to increases 2008/2009 – 2014 whilst cereal production fluctuates
> - 2014 – 2016 fertiliser decreases whilst cereal production increases
> - Positive relationship/both increased until 2014
> - 2008/2009 fertiliser overtook cereal production
> - 2014/2015 crop production overtook fertiliser
> - Max 1 data mark for the following
> - 2004 – 2008 fertiliser 410–420 to 480 kg and cereal production 420 to 490m metric tonnes
> - 2008 – 2014 fertiliser 480 to 560–570 kg and cereal production 490 to 550m metric tonnes
> - 2014 – 2016 fertiliser 560–570 to 500–510 kg and cereal production 550 to 610–620m metric tonnes

> **[exam-tip]**
> It is essential to identify the relationship between crop production and fertiliser. You do not need to explain the relationship, but your description must include figures to gain all three marks.

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 6.3, which shows information about grain production in Brazil between 1990 and 2014.

![qp-6b-0460-w19-qp-11](assets/003-qp-6b-0460-w19-qp-11.png)

Compare the change in grain production in Brazil with the change in the area of land planted with grain and harvested between 1990 and 2014.

You should refer to years and use statistics in your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Both increased but there was a larger increase in production from 55,000 to 195,000 tonnes** [1]** than in harvested area which only increased from 35,000 to 57,000 hectares**[1]** 
Increase in production fluctuates whereas the increase in harvest area is steady [**1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is **'compare'**; means the answer needs to identify both similarities and differences between two or more things.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark **[1]** for each valid point (up to a maximum of 3 marks)
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Little change in harvested area
> - Increase in production goes up and down
> - Harvest area  which does not alter much

> **[exam-tip]**
> Remember to achieve full marks on this question it is essential to include supporting statistics which need to be comparative and must use `tonnes’ and `hectares’ somewhere in answer

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 5.2, which is a graph showing information about the world production of wheat and rice between 1980 and 2013.

![q5-5b-0460-w19-qp-13](assets/004-q5-5b-0460-w19-qp-13.png)

Compare the world production of wheat and rice between 1980 and 2013. You should use statistics in your answer.
parts.solution_md:
In 1980, 430 millions of tonnes of wheat was produced compared to 263 million tonnes of rice [1] 
Both have increased over the time period **[1]** 
There is more fluctuation in the production of wheat than rice [**1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is **'compare'**; means the answer needs to identify both similarities and differences between two or more things.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark **[1]** for each valid point (up to a maximum of 3 marks)
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Both highest in 2013
> - The production of wheat goes up and down more than rice
> - There is more instability in the production of wheat than rice
> - Statistics: (millions of tonnes) 
> 1980                   2013 
> 260/263    462/465 rice 
> 425/430    657/660 wheat

> Remember the answer needs to refer to statistics and give the unit of measurement (millions of tonnes).

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 6.3, which shows recommendations which agricultural experts have given to subsistence farmers in areas such as the one shown in Fig. 6.1. | **Recommendation 1**

Build a covered, concrete-lined well close to the farm. | |---| | **Recommendation 2**

Put electric fences around the fields of maize and millet. | | **Recommendation 3**

Use some of the land to graze a small herd of goats. | **Fig. 6.3** (i) Explain how each of the three recommendations in Fig. 6.3 may increase the farmers’ food supply. -Build a covered, concrete-lined well close to the farm -Put electric fences around the fields of maize and millet -Use some land to graze a small herd of goats
parts.solution_md:
Building a well will enable farmers to irrigate/water crops (more effectively) **[1]** 
Putting electric fences around fields will prevent animals eating them **[1]** 
Using land to graze goats will provide provide additional milk and meat **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is **'explain'**; this means that the answer needs to give reasons that each idea will increase food supply.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark **[1]** for each valid point (up to a maximum of 3 marks)
> 
> **Common errors**
> 
> Common errors where students lose marks include:
> 
> - Misreading of 'well' as 'wall' so giving reasons that a wall would increase food supply
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Electric fences prevent theft by people or trampling by animals
> - Using land to graze goats will provide manure to increase food supplies

> **[exam-tip]**
> When writing your answer it is essential that you are clear about how each method increases food supply.
